comments.text:
Signature: Mix.Tasks.Spec.CheckTest, "json mode includes a growth finding before the last-line verdict", test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs:69 — Jason.DecodeError, unexpected byte 0x57 ("W") at position 0 of the first captured stdout line.

Evidence:
- Sightings 1-2 (2026-08-31): delta test-critic run and rebase worker full-suite runs; accepted under the flake protocol.
- Sightings 3-4 (2026-09-01): two consecutive full-suite runs in a fresh worktree at 8f370c5, both red on this test only (321 tests + 3 properties otherwise green). The file in isolation is green (11 tests). Never red at an actual merge gate so far.

Deliverable:
Root-cause the interleaving and fix it. The repro is concurrency-dependent: a line starting with "W" (a warning) lands on captured stdout before the JSON report only when the full suite runs async. Two hypotheses to rule in or out: (a) the spec.check subprocess itself writes a warning to stdout ahead of the JSON report in JSON mode — a product defect against the single-stdout-writer contract (warnings belong on stderr in JSON mode); (b) the test's capture picks up output from a sibling async test. If (a), fix the output layer; if (b), fix the test's capture/isolation. Deleting or weakening the first-line-is-JSON assertion is not a fix.

Verification:
- Repro first: demonstrate the failure before the fix (full suite, or the test under induced concurrent load); demonstrate the same procedure green after.
- mix test test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs green.
- Full suite green at least twice post-fix.

Allowed touches: lib/ancora/** (only if the root cause is the product output path), test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs, test/support/**.
Out of scope: weakening the JSON-first-line assertion; unrelated test churn.

Blocks ancora-yzu.15: L13 admission smoke is red on this signature.

Summary: Proved hypothesis (b): the captured child Mix process emitted its own "Waiting for lock on the build directory" bootstrap diagnostic under shared-build contention before Ancora's JSON writer started; no sibling output leaked and the product output layer was not involved. The helper now sets MIX_QUIET=1, which silences Mix diagnostics while preserving direct Ancora stdout, and a regression test fails if that flag is omitted. The unchanged-tree contention repro produced the exact Jason 0x57 failure; after the fix the concurrent 322-test suite and repeated target runs had no JSON failure, with one artificial cross-VM worker later stopping on a separate temp-directory collision.

Executed evidence. (1) Would-fail direction: removed MIX_QUIET from run_mix and reran the new test; it failed with left: ["Waiting for lock on the build directory", "{\"ok\":true}"] vs right: ["{\"ok\":true}"]. The equality assertion also kills the all-silenced mutation, since empty stdout != [json]. (2) Same output path as the real flake: in Elixir 1.18.1 (the toolchain here), the lock message is emitted at mix/project.ex:920 via Mix.shell().info/1, and mix/cli.ex:22 swaps in Mix.Shell.Quiet under MIX_QUIET, whose info/1 is a no-op while error/1 still prints. The test calls the identical API with the identical string, so it exercises the path the flake used without needing induced lock contention. (3) Blanket MIX_QUIET is safe for the rest of the file: every ancora output line the other tests assert on goes through IO.puts (Ancora.Output, verdict.ex:37; [CONFIG] via IO.puts(:stderr,...)), never Mix.shell(); full file is 12/12 green with the env var in place. It also hardens the other 11 subprocess tests, e.g. the one asserting the finding at stdout line 0 would have flaked on the same lock line. No sleeps, synchronous System.cmd, deterministic. Worktree restored byte-identical (git diff empty, status clean).

VERIFY: PASS
Session: 68fab1f9-dfb5-49e0-be76-afa9d2d00f6d
Log: /Users/mz/.claude-personal/projects/-Users-mz-src-ancora/68fab1f9-dfb5-49e0-be76-afa9d2d00f6d.jsonl

Mechanical: diff 8f370c5..HEAD (5ddfbd8) touches only test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs (+14/-1); tree clean before and after, byte-identical post-mutation restore (git diff empty).

Root cause reproduced by execution. The lock-hold and lock-churn probes stayed green because a warm _build/dev never contends: spec.check declares @requirements ["deps.loadpaths"], and deps.loadpaths takes the build lock only when deps need compiling. The real mechanism is child-vs-child racing on a cold/stale _build/dev (children run in dev env; the suite runs in test env). With MIX_QUIET reverted, rm -rf _build/dev + two simultaneous `mix spec.check` runs: loser's stdout began "Waiting for lock on the build directory (held by process 33255)" — byte 0x57 at position 0, the exact flake — and the winner's stdout began "==> earmark_parser / Compiling 3 files (.erl)", a second contamination class through the same Mix.shell().info path. Same race with MIX_QUIET=1: both children's stdout starts with product output. Hypothesis (b) confirmed; (a) refuted — ancora writes stdout only via IO.puts (lib/ancora/output/verdict.ex:37, lib/ancora/output.ex:123), never Mix.shell.

Mutation direction: with the {"MIX_QUIET","1"} tuple deleted, the new regression test goes red: left ["Waiting for lock on the build directory", "{\"ok\":true}"]. Restored; red-green confirmed.

No weakening: the json-mode test still parses hd(output_lines) with Jason.decode! strictly (test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs:99).

MIX_QUIET-vs-lock-line: mix/cli.ex:22 installs Mix.Shell.Quiet at CLI start whose info/1 is a no-op; the lock wait line is Mix.shell().info at mix/project.ex:920 (Elixir 1.18.1). The regression test exercises the identical shell-info path, and my live race showed MIX_QUIET silences both the wait line and deps-compile chatter while IO.puts output survives. Caveat stated honestly: in-harness contention on the json test's own child did not land in a few tries (async setup staggering); the deterministic repro was at the exact child-command level the helper wraps, plus the harness-level red mutation test.

Runs: mix test test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs — 12 tests, 0 failures; mix test --stale — 0 failures; specled_ex spec.validate --root <worktree> — "spec.validate result=pass". Implementer log corroborates a genuine pre-fix red (Jason.DecodeError 0x57, 321 tests 1 failure).
